::: {.page-intro}
Since June 2026 I have used Claude Code, an AI agent that reads files, runs code and writes documents, in my work as an economist at GSMA Intelligence. This site reports what I have done with it, what it was worth, and where it fell short, from a log I keep as I work.
:::

## Why keep this record

1. **To record the AI work itself.** Expanding the team's AI capability is one of my objectives. The log records every piece of work done with an agent: what it was, how long it took, and how good the result was.
2. **To build a repository of AI-engineering knowledge.** Each project records what it learned about building with AI agents: what worked, what failed, and which checks made the agents' output trustworthy. Those lessons are saved, tested on the next project and turned into a playbook, so that my ability to build AI products improves with each one.
3. **To measure AI at work, as an economist would.** The economics of AI asks how it changes tasks, productivity and jobs. My own work is a small, well-documented case: each task is logged with the time it took, an estimate of the time it would have taken without AI, and a quality score.
4. **To share what works with the team.** The aim is to help the team judge where agents add value, and where they do not, before deciding how to use them.

## In numbers

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
summary = FileAttachment("data/summary.json").json()
fmt = d3.format(",")
day = s => d3.utcFormat("%-d %b")(new Date(s))
tip = (text, definition) => `<span class="term" tabindex="0" data-tip="${definition}">${text}</span>`
html`<div class="tiles">
  <div class="tile"><div class="value">${summary.valued_entries}</div>
    <div class="label">${tip("tasks", "One task is one finished piece of work done with the agent, logged with my hours, an estimate of the hours without AI, a quality score and the outcome.")} with my hours and assessment</div>
    <div class="period">${day(summary.valued_first)} to ${day(summary.valued_last)}</div></div>
  <div class="tile"><div class="value">${fmt(summary.hours_actual_logged)} h</div>
    <div class="label">my time on those tasks</div>
    <div class="period">${day(summary.valued_first)} to ${day(summary.valued_last)}</div></div>
  <div class="tile gold"><div class="value">${summary.hours_saved_lower_bound}–${summary.hours_saved_raw} h</div>
    <div class="label">${tip("saved", "On tasks that would have been done anyway: my estimate of the hours without AI, minus the hours with it. The lower figure counts only estimates I was highly confident in and wrote down within a week of the work.")} on ${summary.substitution_with_numbers} tasks that would have been done anyway</div>
    <div class="period">${day(summary.valued_first)} to ${day(summary.valued_last)}</div></div>
  <div class="tile teal"><div class="value">${fmt(summary.expansion_hours)} h</div>
    <div class="label">on ${summary.expansion_tasks} ${tip("tasks that would not exist without AI", "Expansion: work I would not have done at all without an agent. It has no time-saved figure, because there is nothing to compare it with.")}</div>
    <div class="period">${day(summary.valued_first)} to ${day(summary.valued_last)}</div></div>
  <div class="tile green"><div class="value">${fmt(summary.usage_tool_calls)}</div>
    <div class="label">${tip("agent actions", "An agent action (tool call) is one thing the agent did on its own: reading a file, running code, searching the web, editing a document. Counted from the agent's session logs.")} <span class="status measured">measured</span></div>
    <div class="period">${day(summary.usage_first_day)} to ${day(summary.usage_last_day)}</div></div>
  <div class="tile green"><div class="value">${summary.radar_runs_successful}</div>
    <div class="label">${tip("unattended runs", "Daily runs of the two radars on a schedule, with no one involved: each reads its sources, checks and archives what it finds, and writes a report. Counted from GitHub.")} of the two radars <span class="status measured">measured</span></div>
    <div class="period">${day(summary.radar_runs_first)} to ${day(summary.radar_runs_as_of)}</div></div>
</div>`
```

**Why the periods differ.** I have used the agent since June. The agent deletes its session records after 30 days unless a session is reopened. I first saved them on 8 September, so usage before about 9 August survives only for sessions I reopened later; the oldest is from 22 July. June and most of July are not recorded. Since 8 September everything is kept. My hours and assessments come from the weekly log, which started on 25 September; the first tasks in it date from 10 September. Work from June to early September appears on this site only as measured usage, not as valued tasks.

Hours, time saved and quality are my own estimates; usage and radar runs are measured. Each figure is labelled on the results pages.

## How the evidence is collected

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 6.5
flowchart TB
    work["Work with an AI agent"] --> logs["Session logs<br/>measured: days, messages, agent actions"]
    work --> weekly["Weekly log, every Friday<br/>one row per finished task"]
    logs --> weekly
    weekly --> judge["My judgement per task<br/>hours, hours without AI,<br/>quality, rework, outcome"]
    judge --> ledger["Validated evidence log<br/>one entry per task"]
    ledger --> views["Views: this report,<br/>quarterly reviews"]
    projects["Each project's weekly<br/>lessons on building with agents"] --> kb["Knowledge base and<br/>playbook for new projects"]
```

- **Scripts do the counting.** Usage figures come from the agent's session logs, and the weekly table is built by script.
- **I supply every judgement.** Hours, quality and outcome are mine, entered in a spreadsheet each week. Nothing is estimated by the agent.
- **Failures count.** Shortfalls, rework and below-expectation results are logged as they happen and reported here.
- **Lessons travel.** Each project writes down what it has learned about building with agents, and those lessons are distilled into a playbook any new project can start from.
